test_focus: production telemetry infrastructure — event logging + aggregator + dashboard. The campaign's effectiveness measurements have all been offline (scripted scenarios, blind A/B with Sonnet judge). Phase 25 ships the infrastructure for ONLINE measurement: real dreams fired, real injections, real helped-rates over real user sessions.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

event_kinds: dream_fired — recorded when maybe_dream produces a DreamArtifact
injection_fired — recorded when ImaginationMiddleware._maybe_inject lands a wrapper into the system prompt
injection_helped — recorded when the next response after injection is not error-flagged
implementation.metadata_per_helped: empty (the relationship to prior injection is implicit in ordering)
wiring: dream_engine.maybe_dream — records dream_fired after artifact write, reading category from frontmatter
imagination._maybe_inject — records injection_fired with style + content_category
imagination._record_outcome — records injection_helped when post-injection response is non-error
user_surface: render_dreamscape_telemetry() in dashboard.py — Rich-markup operator view
/dreamscape stats [hours|all] — slash command shows last N hours (default 24) or whole history
Subcommand registered in commands/general.py for autocomplete
tests_cover: Aggregate counts + dreams_by_category + injections_by_style + helped_rate + approx_cost
Helped rate None when no injections

live_demo.name: scratch_phase25_telemetry_demo.py
live_demo.kind: end-to-end exercise — no A/B, just pipeline verification
steps: Fire 2 real dreams via maybe_dream (Haiku calls)
Fire 2 imagination injections (mechanism-only, no real Haiku)
Verify all events landed in JSONL
live_demo.interpretation: The telemetry pipeline works end-to-end. Every dream fired produced a dream_fired event with title + elapsed + category metadata. Every injection produced an injection_fired event with style + content_category metadata. Every successful injection produced an injection_helped event. The aggregator correctly counts + breaks down by category/style. The dashboard render displays the operator-relevant numbers + rates.

what_this_unlocks: Operators can run `/dreamscape stats` in the CLI to see what dreamscape is actually doing in their session: how many dreams fired, what categories, what injection style, what helped rate.
Future research (Phase 28+) can analyze production telemetry to answer 'does dreamscape help my real users on their real work' — the question the campaign's offline measurements can only proxy.
The category + style breakdowns let an operator see WHICH knob is active: e.g. an engineering agent's dreams_by_category should show 'engineering-craft' as the top entry.
The helped_rate at the agent level surfaces the auto-disable feedback loop transparently — Phase 4's auto-disable mechanism reads this rate too; now operators can see it.

feature_verdicts.event_recorder: sings — 10 unit tests pass, file rotation works at 1 MB cap
feature_verdicts.aggregator: sings — counts + rates + cost estimate correct in unit tests + live demo
feature_verdicts.dashboard_view: sings — empty state + populated state render correctly
feature_verdicts.production_readiness: the infrastructure is production-ready; the data is yet to accumulate in real deployments

known_limitations: The injection-helped signal is coarse (keyword scan for 'traceback', 'error', etc. on the next response). Could miss helpful injections whose response happens to mention an error generically.
JSONL doesn't compact — at 1 MB the log rotates to .1; further rotation needs operator action. Reasonable for current scales but worth revisiting if usage grows.
The dashboard render is text-only Rich markup. A future TUI surface could plot trends over time.
Telemetry isn't shipped to a remote backend by default — it lives locally only. Operators who want to aggregate across deployments would need to add an exporter.
verdict: READY TO MERGE — clean infrastructure ship. The data accumulates as users use dreamscape; the campaign's offline measurements are unchanged.
next_steps: Phase 28 (suggested): privacy-respecting telemetry exporter for operators who want to aggregate across deployments (push to local file path / S3 / SQLite).

Phase 29 (suggested): re-validate the campaign's offline findings against real production telemetry once it accumulates. The judge proxy might disagree with real-user signals; that disagreement is itself informative.

Phase 30 (suggested): per-injection-feedback signal beyond keyword failure detection. E.g. did the user explicitly thank the agent, edit the suggested code, accept a tool call without further prompting?
